summary: Sometimes it is too difficult or impossible to hold a company meeting in the usual ways. When this happens, the Tribunal can step in and order a meeting to take place under special rules. The Tribunal can even decide that just one person attending the meeting counts as a valid meeting.
points: Applies when it is impractical to call or conduct any company meeting except an annual general meeting.
The Tribunal can act on its own or when a director or voting member asks it to.
The Tribunal can order a meeting to be called, held, and conducted in any way it thinks fit.
The Tribunal can give extra directions, which can even change the Act's normal rules for meetings.
The Tribunal can direct that a single member present in person or by proxy counts as a full meeting.
Any meeting held following the Tribunal's orders is legally considered a properly conducted company meeting.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited faced a severe internal dispute, and the directors refused to cooperate, making it impossible to hold a general meeting through the normal company procedures. Rahul, a concerned member of the company who had the right to vote, decided to approach the Tribunal for help. The Tribunal reviewed the situation and used its power to order a special meeting. It gave specific directions on how the meeting should be conducted and even ordered that Rahul alone, being present in person, would be deemed to constitute a valid meeting. Because this meeting followed the Tribunal's exact instructions, it was legally recognized as a proper company meeting for all purposes.

terms.meaning: A special judicial body set up to handle legal disputes and matters related to companies.
Too difficult or impossible to do in a practical way.
Acting on its own initiative without anyone asking it to.
A person authorized to represent and vote for a member at a meeting.

watch: Remember that this power does not apply to annual general meetings.
